summary.text: A 4-year-old child presented to the Emergency Room with skin lesions of both legs and the lower abdomen that had been present for 4 weeks, spreading from both lower limbs towards the lower abdomen. A tick had bitten the groin six weeks before presentation. There was no fever or deterioration in well-being, and the child was referred to the Infectious Diseases Outpatient Clinic for suspected Lyme borreliosis.

Examination found painful, brownish, raised lesions over the back of the legs with progressively increasing surrounding redness, induration, tenderness and popliteal lymphadenopathy, with spots on the lower abdomen. The blood count, CRP, fibrinogen and coagulation factors were normal, while Borrelia IgM and IgG were raised on ELISA and the Western blot was positive. Atypical multiple erythema migrans was diagnosed.

Amoxicillin was started at 50 mg/kg body weight/day. The lesions had not progressed after 1 week and showed mild improvement at 2 weeks, and the antibiotic was continued for a total of 4 weeks, resulting in clinical resolution. A pediatric evaluation 6 weeks after the end of therapy showed no skin changes.

summary.text: An 11-year-old boy who had not been chronically ill was referred in March 2021 for suspected borrelial lymphocytoma. His parents had observed ear asymmetry and enlargement of the right ear auricle in November 2020. Topical mupirocin was recommended without improvement, and an ENT specialist referred him for a biopsy, which showed skin with abundant lymphocytic infiltration.

On consultation the right auricle was bigger with a hard, painless, clear bluish-red swelling of the lobe, skin without erythematous change and no enlarged peripheral lymph nodes. ELISA showed IgG 95 AU/mL, positive, with IgM 17 AU/mL, and Western blot IgG was positive. Lyme disease and borrelial lymphocytoma cutis were diagnosed.

Oral amoxicillin 50 mg/kg body weight/day was given and a clear reduction of the ear lobe lesion was seen at follow-up in the third week of treatment. Treatment continued for up to 28 days, and a re-check 6 weeks after antibiotic initiation showed complete resolution of the skin lesion.

summary.text: An 8-year-old girl presented with a 7-month history of indurated plaques of the lower leg. A bluish-red limited skin hardening with itching had developed in December 2021; antihistamines and later local aclometasone cream brought no improvement, and joint and muscle pain of both legs began four months after the skin lesions appeared. Both parents had chronic Lyme disease.

Examination showed atrophic, hypopigmented, indurated plaques with central epidermal defects. Borrelia IgM and IgG were elevated on ELISA with a positive Western blot, and Lyme borreliosis was diagnosed. Routine laboratory tests were without abnormalities, PCR on the skin biopsy did not detect Bb DNA, and histology corresponded to morphea, with localized scleroderma initiated by Bb diagnosed.

Oral cefuroxime 30 mg/kg body weight/day was prescribed and continued for 4 weeks, and she was referred for a skin biopsy. The parents decided not to follow the hospital recommendation to continue dermatological treatment. A control examination after the end of antibiotic therapy showed local improvement, with the interval described differently in the text and the figure caption.
